question: Which is the most common type of budding yeast, capable of fermenting sugar into carbon dioxide and alcohol and commonly used in baking and brewing?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Saccharomyces cerevisiae**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Saccharomyces cerevisiae:**

__
 
• Commonly known as** baker's yeast** or **brewer's yeast**.
 
• It is the **most common** type of** budding yeast**, capable of** fermenting sugar into carbon dioxide** and **alcohol**.
 
• Commonly used in **baking, brewing, and winemaking**.
 
• It has been extensively studied and used as a **model organism** in scientific research.
 
• It has as a **single-celled structure** and is a **eukaryotic microorganism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saccharomyces boulardii:**

 
 
• **​**A probiotic yeast often used to prevent and treat diarrhea
 
• Not a natural component of the human microbiota, but can be taken as a supplement
 
• Believed to help restore the natural balance of gut bacteria
 
• Has been studied for its potential health benefits in gastrointestinal conditions
 
 
 
• **Schizosaccharomyces pombe:**
 
 
• Also known as fission yeast
 
• Used as a model organism in scientific research, particularly in the study of cell division and genetics
 
• Has a similar single-celled structure to Saccharomyces cerevisiae
 
• Used in the production of certain alcoholic beverages in Africa and Asia
 
 
 
• **Candida albicans:**
 
 
• **​**A type of yeast that is a natural part of the human microbiota
 
• Can cause infections, particularly in immunocompromised individuals
 
• Found in the mouth, digestive tract, and genital area
 
• Overgrowth of Candida albicans can lead to conditions such as thrush and vaginal yeast infections
